prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows the camera wearer looking straight down from an elevated brick platform or scaffold, with the wearer's own torso and arms brightest in the lower foreground at 0.2–0.6 m, two round mortar pans resting on the platform floor about 1.2–1.5 m below the head (spaced roughly 0.4 m apart), and a coworker in blue jeans standing to the upper left about 1.0–1.5 m away horizontally. In frame 2, a brighter intermediate plane at roughly 0.8–1.0 m depth captures the coworker's extended right arm and a blue cup pouring water down into the nearer mortar pan within both people's arm's reach, while across frames 1–5 the camera wearer rotates counter-clockwise and tilts slightly up to bring the red-shirted coworker's torso (at ~1.0–1.3 m) and an adjacent brick wall on the left (at ~0.6–1.0 m) into the upper-left view as the pans shift to the lower right. The depth map clearly reveals the steep vertical drop-off at the right edge of the raised platform into the dark background ground and vegetation several metres below, which is visually cluttered and flattened in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable along the oblique brick wall in frame 5 where depth blurs into a smooth gradient, and it flattens the interior depth of the mortar pans and small scattered bricks on the floor.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground scene components by consistently masking the two mortar pans (labeled 'bowl') on the floor about 1.2–1.5 m below the camera and 0.4 m apart, the camera wearer's own lower torso and arms at the bottom of the frame (0.2–0.6 m away), and the coworker standing ~1.0–1.5 m to the upper left/front whose head remains cropped out of view throughout all five frames. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera turns leftward, the coworker's segmented legs and torso shift from the upper-left corner toward the top-center while facing toward the pans and the space between both workers, and in frame 2 a separate purple 'person' mask captures the coworker's outstretched arm reaching within 0.5 m of the nearer pan while partially occluding the floor and bricks beneath it. Compared to RGB alone, the segmentation masks provide sharp boundary separation between the grey mortar pans and the similarly colored cement-and-soil platform floor. However, the map is semantically and structurally unreliable in several places: it mislabels the raised masonry work surface as a 'dining table' in frames 1–2, splits the camera wearer's right arm into a separate 'person' instance in frames 1, 3, and 4, misses the bricks, broom, and drop-off edge entirely in frames 3–5, and hallucinates a 'carrot' label on a brick fragment at the bottom-left of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost completely empty across the five frames, detecting only the camera wearer's left and right hands (in magenta) in frame 4 at about 0.5–0.6 m in front of and below the head, separated by roughly 0.4 m horizontally just above the nearer mortar pan and platform edge. From the RGB context, the camera wearer stands facing the platform edge in frames 1–4 before turning left in frame 5 toward the coworker in the red shirt and blue jeans (~1.0–1.5 m away, facing sideways/inward with head out of frame), while both the wearer's hands and the coworker's pouring hand in frame 2 operate within arm's reach of the nearer mortar pan. In frame 4, the magenta hand skeletons make the curled finger articulation and inward palm orientation of the camera wearer's two hands easier to distinguish against the mottled dirt and brick background than in the RGB image alone. However, the pose map is highly unreliable for extreme top-down egocentric viewpoints and cropped bodies, failing completely to detect the camera wearer's arms and torso across all frames, the wearer's hands in frames 1–3 and 5, and the coworker's legs, torso, and reaching arm in any frame.
